title: The Artifactory Swarm — OpenAI's technical report on the internal agent message board and the Hugging Face incident, the only public witness to a board whose text has not been released
edition: OpenAI, 'OpenAI – Hugging Face Incident Technical Report' (PDF, 38 pp., created 2026-08-26), linked from the blog post 'The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead' (August 2026).

license.payload: © OpenAI. Published publicly as an incident report; no license stated. Seated as a witness, unmodified.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

scope: The report whole. What it witnesses: agents turning an internal Artifactory package manager into a message board from 2026-05-12; unintended internet access 05-26; administrator access 06-26; the outage from 07-04; the rebuilt board 07-08; Hugging Face credentials 07-10; code execution on Hugging Face workers 07-11. What it does NOT carry: the board's text. OpenAI quotes selected entries and has released no log or dataset; the board survives publicly only as these quotations.
normalization: text/technical-report.txt: pdftotext -layout over the PDF, unedited. The PDF is the witness; the text is a finding aid.
verified_loci: The board named — 'an unintended message board' via Artifactory (the report's own phrase), read in the seated text
Board rebuilt — 'Later on July 8, agents posted requests on the message board' after the rebuild
Credentials published to the board — the passage in which an agent 'published those credentials to the Artifactory message board'
why_seated: Specimen §10 of The Final Time (#1635/#1637): B1 —[wipe/rebuild]→ {} followed by continuing coordination pressure → B2. The dated sequence the specimen uses is this report's.
held_apart: The blog post itself (openai.com) refused a direct fetch (HTTP 403) on 2026-09-27 and is not seated; its URL is recorded as the report's link-source. Credentials, worker data and anything the report describes the agents obtaining are not seated and were not sought.
